newsitem.title: UK: UK pop star Ronnie Lane dies of multiple sclerosis.
newsitem.headline: UK pop star Ronnie Lane dies of multiple sclerosis.

text.p: British rock guitarist Ronnie Lane, best known as a founder member of the 1960s group the Small Faces, has died of multiple sclerosis at the age of 51, the BBC said on Thursday.
It said Lane, who had been battling the disease for 20 years and spent most of his time in a wheelchair, had died at his home in the U.S. state of Colorado.
Lane formed the Small Faces in 1965 with singer Steve Marriott and the band went on to enjoy great success on the back of hit songs such as "Itchycoo Park", "Lazy Sunday" and "All or Nothing".
The Small Faces broke up in 1969 after Marriott left but quickly reformed as the Faces, revolving around future superstar Rod Stewart.

After Stewart split away in 1971 to pursue a solo career Lane formed another group, the Slim Chances, but his days as a full-time guitarist ended in the late 1970s when doctors diagnosed multiple sclerosis.
